body:
What the page paints and what the scene lays out are two answers to the same question, and they had come apart. The page draws its own words through the browser and looks right; the scene -- which lays the boxes out and answers every press -- sized each text by the children it does not have, a text holding nothing, and so threw away the size its own measure had just worked out. A line of text stood at no width and no height in the scene, and every box around one collapsed to its padding: a press reached no node wherever the words were, however well they read.

Two of those nodes are mended already on main -- the fold above an answer and the chips, each given its size by hand (`f79288a`, `ada774b`) -- and the open item that came with them says the rest were found neither fixed nor probed. This is the rest: forty-three `apply` fields across nine `ui` files where the same fault stood -- bubbles and their times, drawer titles, settings' names and values, the top bar's labels, the prompt's heads, captions and doc lines -- each losing its `.autoSize` and nothing else, so the size `measure()` already computes for a text is the size its box takes, the way skiff's own widgets carry their texts. The boxes that hold texts keep auto-sizing to the children they have.

Verified against a build of this very tree -- main merged in, the probe workflow asked by hand: the walk across the fold's pill flips at every step from its left edge to its right, the press a reader gives on the line's own words opens the fold, and nothing the page says complains -- https://github.com/progressive-chat/progressive-chat/actions/runs/42375122725

The probe that found all this was asked by hand the same way (`tools/probe_fold.mjs`, its walk across the pill); a narrower probe of the fold itself landed in `caecd4b`, and this sits beside it.
title: the words size themselves, and the boxes around them hold that size
